statedAs.text: Hunters and anglers in Alberta must have a 10-digit wildlife identification number (WiN) to apply for draws, purchase wildlife certificates, licences and replacements.

statedAs.text: It is unlawful to hunt within 365 metres (400 yards) of the centre-line of the road in a designated road corridor wildlife sanctuary (a corridor 730 metres or 800 yards wide). There are 11 road corridor wildlife sanctuaries.

requirements.citation: 2026 Alberta Guide to Hunting Regulations, road corridor wildlife sanctuaries

restrictionScope.statedAs: Each sanctuary is described by highway segment and centre-line distance, naming no wildlife management unit.

unresolved: The 11 sanctuaries are described by highway segment, so North Ground cannot place a point in one. They are UNLISTED in the within-zone model and must surface as unknown rather than be dropped.

placement.reason: The 11 sanctuaries are described as segments of named highways with stated distances either side of the centre line. That is a linear buffer over road geometry, which is derivable in principle — Alberta publishes its highway network — rather than an area nobody can obtain.
placement.blocker: No dataset of the sanctuary polygons themselves has been located, and deriving them from highway centrelines would be North Ground drawing a regulatory boundary, which §41A forbids. What would close it is an authoritative polygon set, or the authority confirming the buffer construction.

statedAs.text: Persons hunting big game must use an authorized bow and an authorized arrow. An authorized bow is one that is held, drawn and released by muscular power and has a draw weight of not less than 16 kilograms (35 pounds). This is the number of kilograms (pounds) required to draw an arrow of 71 cm (28 inches) to its head. An authorized arrow is one that is not less than 61 cm (24 inches) in length.

requirements.citation: 2026 Alberta Guide to Hunting Regulations, archery equipment

statedAs.text: Persons hunting big game with a crossbow must use an authorized crossbow and arrow (bolt). An authorized crossbow is one that requires 45.4 kilograms (100 pounds) or more of pull to draw the string or cable to its cocked position. There is no restriction on arrow length, however it must have a tip that bears a head that is not intentionally designed to resist being withdrawn after it has penetrated an object.

requirements.citation: 2026 Alberta Guide to Hunting Regulations, crossbow equipment
unresolved: The guide also states 'Crossbows may not be used to hunt big game during arche[ry seasons]' — a season-scoped prohibition recorded here as unresolved because the sentence was truncated in extraction and must be re-read before being encoded as a rule.

laneNotes: Alberta's certified species are three grouse and white-tailed deer. Rows are scoped to those.

The migratory-bird non-toxic shot rule and the CFB Wainwright non-toxic requirement do NOT reach these species: grouse are upland game birds, not migratory, and Wainwright is a base-specific rule. Recorded here so a later reader does not mistake the guide's two non-toxic mentions for a general ammunition restriction.

METHODS is deliberately NOT certified from these rows. They specify what an authorized bow, arrow and crossbow ARE — equipment specifications — not which implements may be used for a given species and season. A specification of an implement is not a permission to use it.
